label: e4b-decontaminated
n_ctx_note: Chat context granted for this run, read from the daemon log ('Creating chat LlamaContext (n_ctx=32768...)'). Well above the ~6600-token agent system prompt, so this run was not context-starved - the failure mode where every turn dies on 'Context window exceeded' and no-tool assertions score as passes.
note: Honest baseline: measured AFTER eval-prompt contamination was removed from agent guidance. Recorded on a purged database so every prompt/skill node was reseeded from the compiled constants - a reused DB keeps old seeded guidance and silently measures the pre-fix prompts. Not comparable to the earlier 11/12, which was measured with eval prompts planted in the guidance. EFFECTIVE SCORE IS 8/12: scenario 3 passes only because the assertion cannot see that its create_schema call failed validation (see caveats[0]). When #1775 lands and scenario 3 passes for real, this headline may not move - compare effective_passed, not the raw count.
caveats: Scenario 3 is a FALSE PASS in this run. Its assertion (noExtraTypes) only checks that create_schema was called once; it does not check the schema persisted. Here create_schema returned is_error=true (title_template placeholders with no fields array) and no equipment type was registered. Scenario 4 then correctly reported the type did not exist and was scored a failure for it. Tracked in #1775.

Scenarios 4 and 6 are downstream of scenario 3's silent failure, not independent defects. 8c is independent and real, but is NOT a blind-retry / IDENTICAL TOOL CALLS violation: the log shows create_node called first with EMPTY arguments (is_error=true, 'missing field node_type'), then corrected and retried successfully. The two calls were not identical, and the recovery itself was reasonable. The actual defect is emitting a tool call with no arguments - the same argument-construction failure class as scenario 3's title_template-without-fields. The toolOnce assertion counts tool NAMES, so it cannot tell a duplicate write from a successful recovery. Tracked in #1775.

Control experiments run after this baseline, recorded so the 8a/8b wording is not re-litigated from git archaeology. (a) The DATABASE=SCHEMA rule is not a literal lookup on the four words database/track/tracker/list: two phrasings lacking all four ('Set up somewhere to note down albums I mean to listen to', 'I want a place to jot down albums worth hearing') both fired create_schema. Do NOT read this as 'the rule generalizes' broadly - both probes are still canonical record-keeping English, n=2 with a stochastic sampler, and neither reaches semantically oblique phrasing. Critically, the FIRST probe string is the exact wording that FAILED as scenario 8a in this run: same prompt, both outcomes. That makes scenario 8a non-deterministic, which is itself a finding. The probes ran single-turn on a fresh chat while 8a runs as the first turn of a multi-turn group, so they do not reproduce the failing condition and cannot attribute the difference to wording vs. context vs. sampling noise. (b) Scenario 4's wording is not the cause - any instance phrasing fails when no schema exists to instantiate.
